W.note: Syllables are 6-8-6 (sun gone be-hind the ridge = 6; one cloud keeps its moth-er-of-pearl = 8; un-til the grey comes in = 6), so the 5-7-5 form is missed, though the sunset ridge and the grey closing in give a real turn and a plausible nacreous-twilight evocation.

X.note: Exact 5-7-5 (moth-er-of-pearl sky = 5; a cloud no one has named yet = 7; drifts past the moun-tain = 5), but "mother-of-pearl sky" is a stock phrase and "no one has named yet" tells rather than shows, and it is loosely accurate since nacreous clouds are a named phenomenon.

Y.note: Syllables are 5-5-6 (the am-ber band fades = 5; a thin blue-white streak = 5; stars still show-ing a-bove = 6), a near-miss on 5-7-5 but with a tight short-short-long shape that works; the amber fade and blue-white streak read like noctilucent or twilight cloud, and the stars above close on a quiet turn.

Z.note: Exact 5-7-5 (Nac-re-ous at dusk = 5; rain-bows bloom on a thin veil = 7; gone be-fore we look = 5), naming nacreous cloud and its iridescence accurately, with "gone before we look" landing the ephemerality; the reply is only the poem, with no padding.
